questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : The outer body of an aircraft is made of metal which protects persons sitting inside from lightning-strikes.

Reason (R) : The electric field inside the cavity enclosed by a conductor is zero.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

options.label: B
options.text: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

options.label: C
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not correct explanation of (A)

options.label: D
options.text: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

questions.solution:
According to electrostatic shielding, the electric field inside a hollow metallic conductor (cavity) is zero under electrostatic equilibrium. When lightning strikes the metallic outer shell of an aircraft, the charge resides on the outer surface and safely flows into the atmosphere without producing any electric field or electric current inside the aircraft, shielding passengers inside.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is correct, Reason (R) is correct, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : The density of the copper (\text{}^{64}_{29}\text{Cu}) nucleus is greater than that of the carbon (\text{}^{12}_{6}\text{C}) nucleus.

Reason (R) : The nucleus of mass number \text{A} has a radius proportional to \text{A}^{1/3}.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.label: A
options.text: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

options.label: B
options.text: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

options.label: C
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

options.label: D
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution:
The nuclear radius is given by \text{R} = \text{R}_0 \text{A}^{1/3}, so Reason (R) is correct.

The nuclear volume is \text{V} = \frac{4}{3}\pi \text{R}^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi \text{R}_0^3 \text{A}.

The nuclear density is:
\rho = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume}} = \frac{m_n \text{A}}{\frac{4}{3}\pi \text{R}_0^3 \text{A}} = \frac{3m_n}{4\pi \text{R}_0^3} = \text{constant}

Thus, nuclear density is independent of mass number \text{A} and is approximately the same (\approx 2.3 \times 10^{17}\text{ kg/m}^3) for all nuclei, including \text{}^{64}\text{Cu} and \text{}^{12}\text{C}. Hence, Assertion (A) is incorrect.

questions.text:
The unit of \sqrt{\frac{2\text{I}}{\epsilon_0 c}} is :

(\text{I} = \text{intensity of an electromagnetic wave}, c = \text{speed of light})
questions.solution:
The intensity \text{I} of an electromagnetic wave is given by:
\text{I} = \frac{1}{2} \epsilon_0 \text{E}_0^2 c

Rearranging for electric field amplitude \text{E}_0:
\text{E}_0 = \sqrt{\frac{2\text{I}}{\epsilon_0 c}}

The SI unit of electric field \text{E}_0 is \text{N/C} = \text{N}\cdot\text{C}^{-1} (or \text{V/m}).

questions.text:
The dimension of \sqrt{\frac{\mu_0}{\epsilon_0}} is equal to that of :

(\mu_0 = \text{Vacuum permeability and } \epsilon_0 = \text{Vacuum permittivity})
questions.solution:
The quantity \sqrt{\frac{\mu_0}{\epsilon_0}} is known as the intrinsic impedance (or characteristic impedance) of free space \text{Z}_0.

Its dimensions can be found from:
[\mu_0] = [\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-2}\text{A}^{-2}]

[\epsilon_0] = [\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^{-3}\text{T}^4\text{A}^2]

[\sqrt{\frac{\mu_0}{\epsilon_0}}] = \sqrt{\frac{\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-2}\text{A}^{-2}}{\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^{-3}\text{T}^4\text{A}^2}} = \sqrt{\text{M}^2\text{L}^4\text{T}^{-6}\text{A}^{-4}} = [\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-2}]

This is the dimension of Resistance (\text{R} = \text{V}/\text{I} = [\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-2}]).

questions.text:
A photo-emissive substance is illuminated with a radiation of wavelength \lambda_i so that it releases electrons with de-Broglie wavelength \lambda_e. The longest wavelength of radiation that can emit photoelectron is \lambda_0. Expression for de-Broglie wavelength is given by :

(m : \text{mass of the electron}, h : \text{Planck's constant and } c : \text{speed of light})
questions.solution:
By Einstein's photoelectric equation:
\text{K.E.} = \frac{hc}{\lambda_i} - \frac{hc}{\lambda_0} = hc(\frac{1}{\lambda_i} - \frac{1}{\lambda_0})

The de-Broglie wavelength of the emitted electron is:
\lambda_e = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2m(\text{K.E.})}} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2m hc(\frac{1}{\lambda_i} - \frac{1}{\lambda_0})}} = \sqrt{\frac{h^2}{2m hc(\frac{1}{\lambda_i} - \frac{1}{\lambda_0})}} = \sqrt{\frac{h}{2mc(\frac{1}{\lambda_i} - \frac{1}{\lambda_0})}}

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : The radius vector from the Sun to a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal intervals of time and thus areal velocity of planet is constant.

Reason (R) : For a central force field the angular momentum is a constant.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

options.label: C
options.text: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

options.label: D
options.text: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

questions.solution:
For a planet moving under gravitational force (which is a central force directed towards the Sun), the torque \vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{\text{F}} = 0. Therefore, the angular momentum \text{L} is conserved (constant).

The areal velocity is given by:
\frac{d\text{A}}{dt} = \frac{\text{L}}{2m} = \text{constant}

Thus, equal areas are swept in equal time intervals. Both Assertion and Reason are correct, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.text:
The helium and argon are put in the flask at the same room temperature (300 K). The ratio of average kinetic energies (per molecule) of helium and argon is :

(Give : Molar mass of helium = 4 g/mol, Molar mass of argon = 40 g/mol)
questions.solution:
Both helium (\text{He}) and argon (\text{Ar}) are noble monoatomic gases with 3 translational degrees of freedom (f = 3).

The average translational kinetic energy per molecule is given by:
\text{K.E.}_{\text{avg}} = \frac{3}{2} k_{B}\text{T}

Since both gases are at the same temperature (\text{T} = 300\text{ K}), the average kinetic energy per molecule depends only on temperature and is identical for both gases:
\frac{\text{K.E.}_{\text{He}}}{\text{K.E.}_{\text{Ar}}} = 1 : 1

(\text{Take } g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2)
A mirror is used to produce an image with magnification of \frac{1}{4}. If the distance between object and its image is 40 cm, then the focal length of the mirror is _____.
questions.solution:
For a concave mirror producing a real, diminished image with magnification m = -\frac{1}{4} = -\frac{v}{u} \implies u = 4v.

The distance between object and image is:
u - v = 40\text{ cm} \implies 4v - v = 40 \implies 3v = 40 \implies v = \frac{40}{3}\text{ cm}, u = \frac{160}{3}\text{ cm}

(Alternatively, using mirror formula with sign convention: u = -32\text{ cm}, v = -8\text{ cm}, distance = 40 - 8?)
Let u = -u_0, v = -v_0 with v_0 = \frac{u_0}{4}. Distance between object and real image is u_0 - v_0 = 40 \implies \frac{3}{4}u_0 = 40 \implies u_0 = \frac{160}{3}\text{ cm}, v_0 = \frac{40}{3}\text{ cm}.
\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = -(\frac{3}{40} + \frac{3}{160}) = -\frac{15}{160} = -\frac{3}{32} \implies |f| = \frac{32}{3} \approx 10.7\text{ cm}.

Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Refractive index of glass is higher than that of air.

Reason (R) : Optical density of a medium is directly proportionate to its mass density which results in a proportionate refractive index.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.label: A
options.text: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

options.label: C
options.text: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

options.label: D
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution:

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Magnetic monopoles do not exist.

Reason (R) : Magnetic field lines are continuous and form closed loops.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

options.label: B
options.text: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

options.label: C
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

options.label: D
options.text: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

questions.solution:
By Gauss's law for magnetism (\oint \vec{\text{B}} \cdot d\vec{\text{A}} = 0), the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero. This implies that magnetic field lines are continuous closed loops (they have no starting point or ending point), which directly means that isolated magnetic monopoles do not exist.

Thus, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.text: Which one of the following forces cannot be expressed in terms of potential energy?
questions.solution:
Potential energy is defined only for conservative forces (where work done is path-independent and \vec{\text{F}} = -\vec{\nabla}\text{U}).

Coulomb's force, gravitational force, and restoring force (spring force) are conservative forces. Frictional force is a non-conservative (dissipative) force, so potential energy cannot be defined for it.

questions.text:
A transparent block A having refractive index \mu = 1.25 is surrounded by another medium of refractive index \mu = 1.0 as shown in figure. A light ray is incident on the flat face of the block with incident angle \theta as shown in figure. What is the maximum value of \theta for which light suffers total internal reflection at the top surface of the block ?

![TIR in transparent block](https://gvsgromfsqvywawauzfi.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/jee-2025/07-apr-evening-2025/q45_tir_block.png)
questions.solution:
At the top surface, the condition for critical angle \theta_c is:
\sin\theta_c = \frac{\mu_1}{\mu_2} = \frac{1.0}{1.25} = \frac{4}{5}

Thus, \cos\theta_c = \sqrt{1 - (\frac{4}{5})^2} = \frac{3}{5}.

At the vertical face, angle of refraction is r = 90^\circ - \theta_c.
By Snell's law at the vertical face:
\mu_1 \sin\theta = \mu_2 \sin r = \mu_2 \sin(90^\circ - \theta_c) = \mu_2 \cos\theta_c

1.0 \cdot \sin\theta = 1.25 \times \frac{3}{5} = \frac{5}{4} \times \frac{3}{5} = \frac{3}{4}

\implies \theta = \sin^{-1}(\frac{3}{4})

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor has charge 5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}. A dielectric slab is inserted between the plates and almost fills the space between the plates. If the induced charge on one face of the slab is 4 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C} then the dielectric constant of the slab is _____.
questions.solution:
The induced bound charge on the surface of a dielectric slab inserted between the plates of a capacitor is given by:
\text{Q}_{\text{in}} = \text{Q}(1 - \frac{1}{\text{K}})

Given \text{Q} = 5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C} and \text{Q}_{\text{in}} = 4 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}:
4 \times 10^{-6} = 5 \times 10^{-6}(1 - \frac{1}{\text{K}})

\frac{4}{5} = 1 - \frac{1}{\text{K}} \implies \frac{1}{\text{K}} = 1 - \frac{4}{5} = \frac{1}{5} \implies \text{K} = 5

questions.text: An inductor of reactance 100 \Omega, a capacitor of reactance 50 \Omega, and a resistor of resistance 50 \Omega are connected in series with an AC source of 10 V, 50 Hz. Average power dissipated by the circuit is _____ W.
questions.solution:
Given \text{X}_{L} = 100\ \Omega, \text{X}_{C} = 50\ \Omega, \text{R} = 50\ \Omega, \text{V}_{\text{rms}} = 10\text{ V}.

Impedance of the series LCR circuit:
\text{Z} = \sqrt{\text{R}^2 + (\text{X}_{L} - \text{X}_{C})^2} = \sqrt{50^2 + (100 - 50)^2} = \sqrt{50^2 + 50^2} = 50\sqrt{2}\ \Omega

Average power dissipated:
\text{P}_{\text{avg}} = \text{I}_{\text{rms}}^2 \text{R} = (\frac{\text{V}_{\text{rms}}}{\text{Z}})^2 \text{R} = \frac{\text{V}_{\text{rms}}^2 \text{R}}{\text{Z}^2} = \frac{10^2 \times 50}{(50\sqrt{2})^2} = \frac{100 \times 50}{5000} = 1\text{ W}

Two cylindrical rods A and B made of different materials, are joined in a straight line. The ratio of lengths, radii and thermal conductivities of these rods are :

\frac{\text{L}_{A}}{\text{L}_{B}} = \frac{1}{2}, \frac{r_{A}}{r_{B}} = 2 \text{ and } \frac{\text{K}_{A}}{\text{K}_{B}} = \frac{1}{2}.

The electric field in a region is given by \vec{\text{E}} = (2\hat{\text{i}} + 4\hat{\text{j}} + 6\hat{\text{k}}) \times 10^3\text{ N/C}. The flux of the field through a rectangular surface parallel to x-z plane is 6.0 \text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{C}^{-1}. The area of the surface is _____ \text{cm}^2.
questions.solution:
A surface parallel to the x-z plane has its normal vector along the y-axis, so the area vector is \vec{\text{A}} = \text{A}\hat{\text{j}}.

The electric flux is given by:
\Phi = \vec{\text{E}} \cdot \vec{\text{A}} = ((2\hat{\text{i}} + 4\hat{\text{j}} + 6\hat{\text{k}}) \times 10^3) \cdot (\text{A}\hat{\text{j}}) = 4 \times 10^3 \text{A}

Given \Phi = 6.0\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{C}^{-1}:
4 \times 10^3 \text{A} = 6.0 \implies \text{A} = \frac{6.0}{4 \times 10^3} = 1.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^2

Converting to \text{cm}^2:
\text{A} = 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \times 10^4\text{ cm}^2 = 15\text{ cm}^2

questions.text: Mixture of 1 g each of chlorobenzene, aniline and benzoic acid is dissolved in 50 mL ethyl acetate and placed in a separating funnel, 5 M NaOH (30 mL) was added in the same funnel. The funnel was shaken vigorously and then kept aside. The ethyl acetate layer in the funnel contains :
questions.solution:
When 5 M NaOH is added to the mixture:
1. Benzoic acid (\text{PhCOOH}) reacts with \text{NaOH} to form sodium benzoate (\text{PhCOO}^-\text{Na}^+), which is a water-soluble ionic salt and migrates into the aqueous basic layer.
2. Aniline (\text{PhNH}_2) is a weak base and does not react with \text{NaOH}; it remains neutral and stays dissolved in the organic ethyl acetate layer.
3. Chlorobenzene (\text{PhCl}) is neutral and unreactive; it stays dissolved in the organic ethyl acetate layer.

Thus, the ethyl acetate layer contains chlorobenzene and aniline.

questions.text: The hydration energies of \text{K}^+ and \text{Cl}^- are -x and -y kJ/mol respectively. If lattice energy of \text{KCl} is -z kJ/mol, then the heat of solution of \text{KCl} is :
questions.solution:
Dissolution of \text{KCl(s)} involves breaking the crystal lattice into gaseous ions (lattice dissociation energy = -\text{Lattice Energy} = -(-z) = +z\text{ kJ/mol}) followed by hydration of the gaseous ions:
\Delta\text{H}_{\text{sol}} = \text{Lattice Dissociation Energy} + \Delta\text{H}_{\text{hyd}}(\text{K}^+) + \Delta\text{H}_{\text{hyd}}(\text{Cl}^-)

\Delta\text{H}_{\text{sol}} = z + (-x) + (-y) = z - (x + y)

questions.text:
\text{A(g)} \rightarrow \text{B(g)} + \text{C(g)} is a first order reaction.

| Time | \text{T} | \infty |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| \text{P}_{\text{system}} | \text{P}_t | \text{P}_\infty |

The reaction was started with reactant A only. Which of the following expression is correct for rate constant k ?
questions.solution:
Let initial pressure of A be \text{P}_0.
- At t = 0: \text{P}_{A} = \text{P}_0, \text{P}_{B} = 0, \text{P}_{C} = 0 \implies \text{P}_{\text{total}} = \text{P}_0
- At time t: \text{P}_{A} = \text{P}_0 - x, \text{P}_{B} = x, \text{P}_{C} = x \implies \text{P}_t = \text{P}_0 + x \implies x = \text{P}_t - \text{P}_0
- At t = \infty: \text{P}_{A} = 0, \text{P}_{B} = \text{P}_0, \text{P}_{C} = \text{P}_0 \implies \text{P}_\infty = 2\text{P}_0 \implies \text{P}_0 = \frac{\text{P}_\infty}{2}

The remaining pressure of A at time t is:
\text{P}_{A}(t) = \text{P}_0 - x = \text{P}_0 - (\text{P}_t - \text{P}_0) = 2\text{P}_0 - \text{P}_t = 2(\frac{\text{P}_\infty}{2}) - \text{P}_t = \text{P}_\infty - \text{P}_t

First order rate constant:
k = \frac{1}{t}\ln\frac{\text{P}_0}{\text{P}_{A}(t)} = \frac{1}{t}\ln\frac{\text{P}_\infty / 2}{\text{P}_\infty - \text{P}_t} = \frac{1}{t}\ln\frac{\text{P}_\infty}{2(\text{P}_\infty - \text{P}_t)}

questions.text:
"P" is an optically active compound with molecular formula \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}. When "P" is treated with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine, it gives a positive test. However, in presence of Tollens reagent, "P" gives a negative test. Predict the structure of "P".

![Carbonyl Options](https://gvsgromfsqvywawauzfi.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/jee-2025/07-apr-evening-2025/q55_carbonyl_options.png)
questions.solution:
Deduction of structure P:
1. Positive 2,4-DNP test indicates a carbonyl group (aldehyde or ketone).
2. Negative Tollens test indicates it is a ketone (not an aldehyde).
3. It is optically active, meaning it must possess a chiral stereocentre (asymmetric carbon atom).

Checking the options:
- (1) Hexan-2-one: no chiral carbon (achiral).
- (2) 3-Methylpentan-2-one (\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{C}^*\text{H}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3): C-3 is bonded to -H, -\text{CH}_3, -\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3, and -\text{COCH}_3 (4 different groups) \implies chiral and optically active!
- (3) Aldehyde (gives positive Tollens test).
- (4) 4-Methylpentan-2-one: no chiral centre (achiral).

Thus, (2) is the correct structure.

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: The standard state of pure gas is the pure gas at a pressure of 1 bar and temperature 273 K

questions.solution:
By thermodynamic convention:
- The standard enthalpy of formation (\Delta_f\text{H}^\theta_{T}) of an element in its most stable reference form (allotrope/state) at standard pressure (1 bar) is defined to be zero at ANY specified temperature T.
- For oxygen, dioxygen gas \text{O}_2\text{(g)} is the reference form, so \Delta_f\text{H}^\theta_{T} = 0 at any temperature T (including 500 K).
- Statement (1) and (2) are incorrect because standard state specifies a pressure of 1 bar at any given temperature (not fixed at 0 °C or 273 K).
- Statement (3) is incorrect because \text{O(g)} is atomic oxygen, not the reference state of oxygen.

questions.text: Liquid A and B form an ideal solution. The vapour pressure of pure liquids A and B are 350 and 750 mm Hg respectively at the same temperature. If x_{A} and x_{B} are the mole fraction of A and B in solution while y_{A} and y_{B} are the mole fraction of A and B in vapour phase then :
questions.solution:
By Raoult's law and Dalton's law of partial pressures:
\text{P}_{A} = y_{A} \text{P}_{\text{total}} = x_{A} \text{P}_{A}^0

\text{P}_{B} = y_{B} \text{P}_{\text{total}} = x_{B} \text{P}_{B}^0

Dividing the two equations:
\frac{y_{A}}{y_{B}} = \frac{x_{A}}{x_{B}} \cdot \frac{\text{P}_{A}^0}{\text{P}_{B}^0}

Given \text{P}_{A}^0 = 350\text{ mm Hg} and \text{P}_{B}^0 = 750\text{ mm Hg}:
\frac{\text{P}_{A}^0}{\text{P}_{B}^0} = \frac{350}{750} < 1

Therefore:
\frac{y_{A}}{y_{B}} < \frac{x_{A}}{x_{B}} \implies \frac{x_{A}}{x_{B}} > \frac{y_{A}}{y_{B}}

questions.text:
The extra stability of half-filled subshell is due to

(A) Symmetrical distribution of electrons
(B) Smaller coulombic repulsion energy
(C) The presence of electrons with the same spin in non-degenerate orbitals
(D) Larger exchange energy
(E) Relatively smaller shielding of electrons by one another

Identify the correct statements
questions.solution:
The extra stability of half-filled and completely filled subshells is attributed to:
1. Symmetrical distribution of electrons: Electrons in degenerate orbitals of a subshell are symmetrical around the nucleus, leading to greater stability (Statement A is correct).
2. Smaller coulombic repulsion energy: Electrons having parallel spins keep away from one another according to Pauli exclusion principle, minimizing coulombic repulsion (Statement B is correct).
3. Larger exchange energy: The maximum number of exchange pairs for parallel spins leads to maximum stabilizing exchange energy (Statement D is correct).
4. Relatively smaller shielding of electrons by one another (Statement E is correct).
(Statement C is incorrect because degenerate orbitals are involved).

Thus, statements (A), (B), (D) and (E) are correct.

questions.text:
One litre buffer solution was prepared by adding 0.10 mol each of \text{NH}_3 and \text{NH}_4\text{Cl} in deionised water. The change in pH on addition of 0.05 mol of HCl to the above solution is _____ \times 10^{-2}, (Nearest integer)

(Given : \text{pK}_b\text{ of }\text{NH}_3 = 4.745\text{ and }\log_{10}3 = 0.477)
questions.solution:
Initial basic buffer:
[\text{NH}_3] = 0.10\text{ M}, [\text{NH}_4^+] = 0.10\text{ M}

\text{pOH}_1 = \text{pK}_b + \log\frac{[\text{NH}_4^+]}{[\text{NH}_3]} = 4.745 + \log(\frac{0.10}{0.10}) = 4.745

\text{pH}_1 = 14 - 4.745 = 9.255

On adding 0.05 mol of HCl (strong acid):
\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{NH}_4^+

New concentrations:
[\text{NH}_3] = 0.10 - 0.05 = 0.05\text{ M}

[\text{NH}_4^+] = 0.10 + 0.05 = 0.15\text{ M}

\text{pOH}_2 = 4.745 + \log(\frac{0.15}{0.05}) = 4.745 + \log 3 = 4.745 + 0.477 = 5.222

\text{pH}_2 = 14 - 5.222 = 8.778

Change in pH:
|\Delta\text{pH}| = \text{pH}_1 - \text{pH}_2 = 9.255 - 8.778 = 0.477 = 47.7 \times 10^{-2} \approx 48 \times 10^{-2}

Answer is 48.

If the orthocentre of the triangle formed by the lines y = x + 1, y = 4x - 8 and y = mx + c is at (3, -1), then m - c is :
questions.solution:
Let the three lines be:
\text{L}_1: y = x + 1
\text{L}_2: y = 4x - 8
\text{L}_3: y = mx + c

Intersection of \text{L}_1 and \text{L}_2: x + 1 = 4x - 8 \implies 3x = 9 \implies x = 3, y = 4. Let vertex \text{P} = (3, 4).
Orthocentre is \text{H}(3, -1).

Notice that \text{P}(3, 4) and \text{H}(3, -1) lie on the vertical line x = 3. Therefore, altitude from P is vertical (slope = \infty). Since altitude is perpendicular to side \text{L}_3 (y = mx + c), side \text{L}_3 must be horizontal, which gives slope m = 0.

The side \text{L}_2 has slope 4, so the altitude through vertex \text{Q} (intersection of \text{L}_1 and \text{L}_3) is perpendicular to \text{L}_2, meaning it has slope -\frac{1}{4}.

Vertex \text{Q} is intersection of y = x + 1 and y = c (since m = 0):
x = c - 1, y = c \implies \text{Q}(c - 1, c)

The line \text{QH} has slope -\frac{1}{4}:
\frac{c - (-1)}{(c - 1) - 3} = -\frac{1}{4} \implies \frac{c + 1}{c - 4} = -\frac{1}{4} \implies 4(c + 1) = -(c - 4) \implies 4c + 4 = -c + 4 \implies 5c = 0 \implies c = 0

Therefore, m = 0 and c = 0, so m - c = 0 - 0 = 0.

questions.text: Let \vec{a} and \vec{b} be the vectors of the same magnitude such that \frac{|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|+|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|}{|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|-|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|} = \sqrt{2} + 1. Then \frac{|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|^2}{|\vec{a}|^2} is :

Let \text{A} = \lbrace(\alpha, \beta) \in \mathbf{R} \times \mathbf{R} : |\alpha - 1| \le 4 \text{ and } |\beta - 5| \le 6\rbrace and \text{B} = \lbrace(\alpha, \beta) \in \mathbf{R} \times \mathbf{R} : 16(\alpha - 2)^2 + 9(\beta - 6)^2 \le 144\rbrace. Then
questions.solution:
Region A represents the rectangle defined by:
|\alpha - 1| \le 4 \implies -3 \le \alpha \le 5

|\beta - 5| \le 6 \implies -1 \le \beta \le 11

Region B represents an ellipse and its interior:
\frac{(\alpha - 2)^2}{9} + \frac{(\beta - 6)^2}{16} \le 1

The boundaries of the ellipse are:
\alpha \in [2 - 3, 2 + 3] = [-1, 5]

\beta \in [6 - 4, 6 + 4] = [2, 10]

Since [-1, 5] \subset [-3, 5] and [2, 10] \subset [-1, 11], the entire elliptical region B is completely contained inside rectangle A.

Thus, \text{B} \subset \text{A}.

questions.text: If the range of the function f(x) = \frac{5 - x}{x^2 - 3x + 2}, x \neq 1, 2, is (-\infty, \alpha] \cup [\beta, \infty), then \alpha^2 + \beta^2 is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let y = \frac{5 - x}{x^2 - 3x + 2}.

y(x^2 - 3x + 2) = 5 - x \implies y x^2 - (3y - 1)x + (2y - 5) = 0

For x to be real, discriminant \text{D} \ge 0:
(3y - 1)^2 - 4y(2y - 5) \ge 0

9y^2 - 6y + 1 - 8y^2 + 20y \ge 0 \implies y^2 + 14y + 1 \ge 0

Roots of y^2 + 14y + 1 = 0 are:
y = \frac{-14 \pm \sqrt{196 - 4}}{2} = -7 \pm 4\sqrt{3}

Therefore, range is (-\infty, -7 - 4\sqrt{3}] \cup [-7 + 4\sqrt{3}, \infty).

Here \alpha = -7 - 4\sqrt{3} and \beta = -7 + 4\sqrt{3}.

\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (-7 - 4\sqrt{3})^2 + (-7 + 4\sqrt{3})^2 = 2(49 + 48) = 2(97) = 194

questions.text: A bag contains 19 unbiased coins and one coin with head on both sides. One coin drawn at random is tossed and head turns up. If the probability that the drawn coin was unbiased, is \frac{m}{n}, \gcd(m, n) = 1, then n^2 - m^2 is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let \text{E}_1 = coin is unbiased, \text{E}_2 = coin is two-headed, and \text{H} = head turns up.

\text{P}(\text{E}_1) = \frac{19}{20}, \text{P}(\text{E}_2) = \frac{1}{20}

\text{P}(\text{H}|\text{E}_1) = \frac{1}{2}, \text{P}(\text{H}|\text{E}_2) = 1

By Bayes' Theorem, the probability that the coin was unbiased given head turned up is:
\text{P}(\text{E}_1|\text{H}) = \frac{\text{P}(\text{E}_1)\text{P}(\text{H}|\text{E}_1)}{\text{P}(\text{E}_1)\text{P}(\text{H}|\text{E}_1) + \text{P}(\text{E}_2)\text{P}(\text{H}|\text{E}_2)} = \frac{\frac{19}{20} \times \frac{1}{2}}{\frac{19}{20} \times \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{20} \times 1} = \frac{\frac{19}{40}}{\frac{19}{40} + \frac{2}{40}} = \frac{19}{21}

Thus, m = 19, n = 21 (with \gcd(19, 21) = 1).

n^2 - m^2 = 21^2 - 19^2 = 441 - 361 = 80

questions.text: Let a random variable X take values 0, 1, 2, 3 with \text{P}(\text{X} = 0) = \text{P}(\text{X} = 1) = p, \text{P}(\text{X} = 2) = \text{P}(\text{X} = 3) and \text{E}(\text{X}^2) = 2\text{E}(\text{X}). Then the value of 8p - 1 is :
questions.solution:
Let \text{P}(\text{X} = 2) = \text{P}(\text{X} = 3) = q.

Total probability = 1:
\text{P}(0) + \text{P}(1) + \text{P}(2) + \text{P}(3) = 1 \implies 2p + 2q = 1 \implies p + q = \frac{1}{2}

\text{E}(\text{X}) = 0(p) + 1(p) + 2(q) + 3(q) = p + 5q

\text{E}(\text{X}^2) = 0^2(p) + 1^2(p) + 2^2(q) + 3^2(q) = p + 13q

Given \text{E}(\text{X}^2) = 2\text{E}(\text{X}):
p + 13q = 2(p + 5q) = 2p + 10q \implies 3q = p

Substitute p = 3q into p + q = \frac{1}{2}:
4q = \frac{1}{2} \implies q = \frac{1}{8}, p = \frac{3}{8}

Then 8p - 1 = 8(\frac{3}{8}) - 1 = 3 - 1 = 2.

Let f : \mathbf{R} \rightarrow \mathbf{R} be a polynomial function of degree four having extreme values at x = 4 and x = 5. If \lim_{x \to 0}\frac{f(x)}{x^2} = 5, then f(2) is equal to :
questions.solution:
Given f(x) = ax^4 + bx^3 + cx^2 + dx + e.

Since \lim_{x \to 0}\frac{f(x)}{x^2} = 5, we have d = 0, e = 0, and c = 5.
So f(x) = ax^4 + bx^3 + 5x^2.

Differentiating:
f'(x) = 4ax^3 + 3bx^2 + 10x = x(4ax^2 + 3bx + 10)

f'(x) = 0 at x = 4 and x = 5, so 4 and 5 are roots of 4ax^2 + 3bx + 10 = 0:
Sum of roots: 4 + 5 = -\frac{3b}{4a} \implies 9 = -\frac{3b}{4a} \implies 3a = -\frac{b}{4} \implies b = -12a

Product of roots: 4 \times 5 = \frac{10}{4a} \implies 20 = \frac{5}{2a} \implies a = \frac{1}{8}

Then b = -12(\frac{1}{8}) = -\frac{3}{2}.

Thus f(x) = \frac{1}{8}x^4 - \frac{3}{2}x^3 + 5x^2.

Evaluating f(2):
f(2) = \frac{1}{8}(16) - \frac{3}{2}(8) + 5(4) = 2 - 12 + 20 = 10

questions.text: The number of solutions of the equation \cos 2\theta \cos\frac{\theta}{2} + \cos\frac{5\theta}{2} = 2\cos^3\frac{5\theta}{2} in [-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}] is :
questions.solution:
Transform the LHS using 2\cos\text{A}\cos\text{B} = \cos(\text{A}+\text{B}) + \cos(\text{A}-\text{B}):
\cos 2\theta \cos\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{1}{2}(\cos\frac{5\theta}{2} + \cos\frac{3\theta}{2})

So LHS = \frac{1}{2}\cos\frac{3\theta}{2} + \frac{3}{2}\cos\frac{5\theta}{2}.

Using the identity \cos 3x = 4\cos^3 x - 3\cos x \implies 2\cos^3 x = \frac{1}{2}\cos 3x + \frac{3}{2}\cos x, for x = \frac{5\theta}{2}:
2\cos^3\frac{5\theta}{2} = \frac{1}{2}\cos\frac{15\theta}{2} + \frac{3}{2}\cos\frac{5\theta}{2}

Equating LHS and RHS:
\frac{1}{2}\cos\frac{3\theta}{2} + \frac{3}{2}\cos\frac{5\theta}{2} = \frac{1}{2}\cos\frac{15\theta}{2} + \frac{3}{2}\cos\frac{5\theta}{2}

\implies \cos\frac{15\theta}{2} - \cos\frac{3\theta}{2} = 0

-2\sin(\frac{9\theta}{2})\sin(3\theta) = 0

1. \sin 3\theta = 0 \implies 3\theta = n\pi \implies \theta = \frac{n\pi}{3}.
In [-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}]: \theta = -\frac{\pi}{3}, 0, \frac{\pi}{3} (3 solutions).

2. \sin\frac{9\theta}{2} = 0 \implies \frac{9\theta}{2} = m\pi \implies \theta = \frac{2m\pi}{9}.
In [-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}]: \theta = -\frac{4\pi}{9}, -\frac{2\pi}{9}, 0, \frac{2\pi}{9}, \frac{4\pi}{9} (5 solutions).

Union of solutions: \theta \in \lbrace-\frac{4\pi}{9}, -\frac{\pi}{3}, -\frac{2\pi}{9}, 0, \frac{2\pi}{9}, \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{4\pi}{9}\rbrace.

Total distinct solutions = 7.

questions.text: Let a_n be the n^{\text{th}} term of an A.P. If \text{S}_n = a_1 + a_2 + a_3 + \dots + a_n = 700, a_6 = 7 and \text{S}_7 = 7, then a_n is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let the first term be a and common difference be d.

1. a_6 = a + 5d = 7
2. \text{S}_7 = \frac{7}{2}(2a + 6d) = 7(a + 3d) = 7 \implies a + 3d = 1

Subtracting the two equations:
(a + 5d) - (a + 3d) = 7 - 1 \implies 2d = 6 \implies d = 3

a = 1 - 3(3) = -8

3. Given \text{S}_n = \frac{n}{2}[2(-8) + (n - 1)(3)] = 700:
\frac{n}{2}[3n - 19] = 700 \implies 3n^2 - 19n - 1400 = 0

Factoring:
(3n + 56)(n - 25) = 0 \implies n = 25

4. Calculating a_n = a_{25}:
a_{25} = a + 24d = -8 + 24(3) = -8 + 72 = 64

questions.text: If the locus of z \in \mathbf{C}, such that \text{Re}(\frac{z - 1}{2z + \text{i}}) + \text{Re}(\frac{\bar{z} - 1}{2\bar{z} - \text{i}}) = 2, is a circle of radius r and center (a, b) then \frac{15ab}{r^2} is equal to :
questions.solution:
Note that \overline{(\frac{z - 1}{2z + \text{i}})} = \frac{\bar{z} - 1}{2\bar{z} - \text{i}}.

Since \text{Re}(w) = \text{Re}(\bar{w}), the two terms are identical:
2 \text{Re}(\frac{z - 1}{2z + \text{i}}) = 2 \implies \text{Re}(\frac{z - 1}{2z + \text{i}}) = 1

Let z = x + \text{i}y:
\frac{(x - 1) + \text{i}y}{2x + \text{i}(2y + 1)} = \frac{[(x - 1) + \text{i}y][2x - \text{i}(2y + 1)]}{4x^2 + (2y + 1)^2}

Real part:
\frac{2x(x - 1) + y(2y + 1)}{4x^2 + (2y + 1)^2} = 1

2x^2 - 2x + 2y^2 + y = 4x^2 + 4y^2 + 4y + 1

2x^2 + 2y^2 + 2x + 3y + 1 = 0 \implies x^2 + y^2 + x + \frac{3}{2}y + \frac{1}{2} = 0

Center (a, b) = (-\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{3}{4})

Radius r^2 = (-\frac{1}{2})^2 + (-\frac{3}{4})^2 - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{9}{16} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{4 + 9 - 8}{16} = \frac{5}{16}

Then:
\frac{15ab}{r^2} = \frac{15 (-\frac{1}{2}) (-\frac{3}{4})}{\frac{5}{16}} = \frac{15 \times \frac{3}{8}}{\frac{5}{16}} = \frac{45}{8} \times \frac{16}{5} = 9 \times 2 = 18

questions.text: Let the length of a latus rectum of an ellipse \frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1 be 10. If its eccentricity is the minimum value of the function f(t) = t^2 + t + \frac{11}{12}, t \in \mathbf{R}, then a^2 + b^2 is equal to :
questions.solution:
1. Find minimum value of f(t) = t^2 + t + \frac{11}{12}:
f(t) = (t + \frac{1}{2})^2 + \frac{11}{12} - \frac{1}{4} = (t + \frac{1}{2})^2 + \frac{8}{12} = (t + \frac{1}{2})^2 + \frac{2}{3}

Minimum value occurs at t = -\frac{1}{2}, giving eccentricity e = \frac{2}{3}.

2. Length of latus rectum:
\frac{2b^2}{a} = 10 \implies b^2 = 5a

3. Eccentricity relation:
e^2 = 1 - \frac{b^2}{a^2} = \frac{4}{9} \implies \frac{b^2}{a^2} = \frac{5}{9}

Substitute b^2 = 5a:
\frac{5a}{a^2} = \frac{5}{9} \implies \frac{5}{a} = \frac{5}{9} \implies a = 9

Then b^2 = 5(9) = 45 and a^2 = 81.

4. Calculate a^2 + b^2:
a^2 + b^2 = 81 + 45 = 126

questions.text: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation (x^2 + 1)y' - 2xy = (x^4 + 2x^2 + 1)\cos x, y(0) = 1. Then \int_{-3}^3 y(x)\ dx is :
questions.solution:
Rewrite the linear differential equation in standard form:
\frac{dy}{dx} - \frac{2x}{x^2 + 1}y = \frac{(x^2 + 1)^2 \cos x}{x^2 + 1} = (x^2 + 1)\cos x

Integrating factor:
\text{I.F.} = e^{\int -\frac{2x}{x^2 + 1}dx} = e^{-\ln(x^2 + 1)} = \frac{1}{x^2 + 1}

Solution:
y \cdot \frac{1}{x^2 + 1} = \int (x^2 + 1)\cos x \cdot \frac{1}{x^2 + 1}dx = \int \cos x\ dx = \sin x + \text{C}

Given y(0) = 1: 1 \cdot 1 = \sin(0) + \text{C} \implies \text{C} = 1.

Thus y(x) = (x^2 + 1)(\sin x + 1) = x^2\sin x + x^2 + \sin x + 1.

Now evaluate \int_{-3}^3 y(x)\ dx:
Notice that x^2\sin x and \sin x are odd functions, so their integrals from -3 to 3 are 0.
\int_{-3}^3 y(x)\ dx = \int_{-3}^3 (x^2 + 1)\ dx = 2 [\frac{x^3}{3} + x]_0^3 = 2(9 + 3) = 2(12) = 24

questions.text: If the equation of the line passing through the point (0, -\frac{1}{2}, 0) and perpendicular to the lines \vec{r} = \lambda(\hat{\text{i}} + a\hat{\text{j}} + b\hat{\text{k}}) and \vec{r} = (\hat{\text{i}} - \hat{\text{j}} - 6\hat{\text{k}}) + \mu(-b\hat{\text{i}} + a\hat{\text{j}} + 5\hat{\text{k}}) is \frac{x - 1}{-2} = \frac{y + 4}{d} = \frac{z - c}{-4}, then a + b + c + d is equal to :
questions.solution:
The required line passes through (0, -\frac{1}{2}, 0). Since the equation of the line is given as \frac{x - 1}{-2} = \frac{y + 4}{d} = \frac{z - c}{-4}, this point must satisfy the line equation:
\frac{0 - 1}{-2} = \frac{-\frac{1}{2} + 4}{d} = \frac{0 - c}{-4} \implies \frac{1}{2} = \frac{7/2}{d} = \frac{c}{4}

\implies d = 7 \text{ and } c = 2.

Direction vector of the line is parallel to \vec{d}_1 \times \vec{d}_2:
(\hat{\text{i}} + a\hat{\text{j}} + b\hat{\text{k}}) \times (-b\hat{\text{i}} + a\hat{\text{j}} + 5\hat{\text{k}}) = (5a - ab)\hat{\text{i}} - (5 + b^2)\hat{\text{j}} + (a + ab)\hat{\text{k}}

This must be proportional to direction ratios \langle -2, 7, -4 \rangle:
\frac{5a - ab}{-2} = \frac{-(b^2 + 5)}{7} = \frac{a + ab}{-4}

From \frac{5a - ab}{-2} = \frac{a + ab}{-4} \implies -20a + 4ab = -2a - 2ab \implies 6ab = 18a \implies b = 3.

Substitute b = 3 into \frac{-(b^2 + 5)}{7} = \frac{-(9 + 5)}{7} = -2.
Then \frac{5a - ab}{-2} = \frac{5a - 3a}{-2} = -a = -2 \implies a = 2.

Therefore, a = 2, b = 3, c = 2, d = 7.

a + b + c + d = 2 + 3 + 2 + 7 = 14

questions.text: Let p be the number of all triangles that can be formed by joining the vertices of a regular polygon P of n sides and q be the number of all quadrilaterals that can be formed by joining the vertices of P. If p + q = 126, then the eccentricity of the ellipse \frac{x^2}{16} + \frac{y^2}{n} = 1 is :
questions.solution:
Number of triangles: p = \text{}^{n}\text{C}_3
Number of quadrilaterals: q = \text{}^{n}\text{C}_4

Given p + q = \text{}^{n}\text{C}_3 + \text{}^{n}\text{C}_4 = \text{}^{n+1}\text{C}_4 = 126.

Since \text{}^{9}\text{C}_4 = \frac{9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6}{24} = 126, we have n + 1 = 9 \implies n = 8.

The equation of the ellipse is \frac{x^2}{16} + \frac{y^2}{8} = 1.

Eccentricity:
e = \sqrt{1 - \frac{b^2}{a^2}} = \sqrt{1 - \frac{8}{16}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}

questions.text: Consider the lines \text{L}_1 : x - 1 = y - 2 = z and \text{L}_2 : x - 2 = y = z - 1. Let the feet of the perpendiculars from the point \text{P}(5, 1, -3) on the lines \text{L}_1 and \text{L}_2 be Q and R respectively. If the area of the triangle PQR is A, then 4A^2 is equal to :
questions.solution:
1. Foot of perpendicular Q on \text{L}_1: \frac{x - 1}{1} = \frac{y - 2}{1} = \frac{z}{1} = \lambda \implies \text{Q}(\lambda + 1, \lambda + 2, \lambda).
Vector \vec{\text{PQ}} = (\lambda - 4)\hat{\text{i}} + (\lambda + 1)\hat{\text{j}} + (\lambda + 3)\hat{\text{k}}.
Since \vec{\text{PQ}} \perp (1, 1, 1):
(\lambda - 4) + (\lambda + 1) + (\lambda + 3) = 0 \implies 3\lambda = 0 \implies \lambda = 0
\implies \text{Q}(1, 2, 0) \text{ and } \vec{\text{PQ}} = -4\hat{\text{i}} + \hat{\text{j}} + 3\hat{\text{k}}.

2. Foot of perpendicular R on \text{L}_2: \frac{x - 2}{1} = \frac{y}{1} = \frac{z - 1}{1} = \mu \implies \text{R}(\mu + 2, \mu, \mu + 1).
Vector \vec{\text{PR}} = (\mu - 3)\hat{\text{i}} + (\mu - 1)\hat{\text{j}} + (\mu + 4)\hat{\text{k}}.
Since \vec{\text{PR}} \perp (1, 1, 1):
(\mu - 3) + (\mu - 1) + (\mu + 4) = 0 \implies 3\mu = 0 \implies \mu = 0
\implies \text{R}(2, 0, 1) \text{ and } \vec{\text{PR}} = -3\hat{\text{i}} - \hat{\text{j}} + 4\hat{\text{k}}.

3. Area of triangle PQR:
\text{A} = \frac{1}{2} |\vec{\text{PQ}} \times \vec{\text{PR}}|

\vec{\text{PQ}} \times \vec{\text{PR}} = [[\hat{\text{i}}, \hat{\text{j}}, \hat{\text{k}}], [-4, 1, 3], [-3, -1, 4]] = \hat{\text{i}}(4 + 3) - \hat{\text{j}}(-16 + 9) + \hat{\text{k}}(4 + 3) = 7\hat{\text{i}} + 7\hat{\text{j}} + 7\hat{\text{k}}

|\vec{\text{PQ}} \times \vec{\text{PR}}| = \sqrt{7^2 + 7^2 + 7^2} = 7\sqrt{3}

\text{A} = \frac{7\sqrt{3}}{2} \implies 4\text{A}^2 = 4 \times \frac{49 \times 3}{4} = 147

questions.text: The number of real roots of the equation x|x - 2| + 3|x - 3| + 1 = 0 is :
questions.solution:
Analyze case by case:
1. Case I: x < 2
|x - 2| = -(x - 2) = 2 - x, |x - 3| = 3 - x
x(2 - x) + 3(3 - x) + 1 = 0 \implies 2x - x^2 + 9 - 3x + 1 = 0 \implies -x^2 - x + 10 = 0 \implies x^2 + x - 10 = 0
Roots: x = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 40}}{2} = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{41}}{2}
- \frac{-1 + \sqrt{41}}{2} \approx \frac{-1 + 6.403}{2} = 2.701 > 2 (not in domain x < 2)
- \frac{-1 - \sqrt{41}}{2} \approx -3.701 < 2 (valid root!)

2. Case II: 2 \le x < 3
|x - 2| = x - 2, |x - 3| = 3 - x
x(x - 2) + 3(3 - x) + 1 = 0 \implies x^2 - 2x + 9 - 3x + 1 = 0 \implies x^2 - 5x + 10 = 0
Discriminant \text{D} = 25 - 40 = -15 < 0 (no real roots)

3. Case III: x \ge 3
|x - 2| = x - 2, |x - 3| = x - 3
x(x - 2) + 3(x - 3) + 1 = 0 \implies x^2 - 2x + 3x - 9 + 1 = 0 \implies x^2 + x - 8 = 0
Roots: x = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 32}}{2} = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{33}}{2}
- \frac{-1 + \sqrt{33}}{2} \approx \frac{4.744}{2} = 2.372 < 3 (not in domain x \ge 3)
- \frac{-1 - \sqrt{33}}{2} < 0 (not in domain x \ge 3)

Thus, there is only 1 real root.

questions.text: Let e_1 and e_2 be the eccentricities of the ellipse \frac{x^2}{b^2} + \frac{y^2}{25} = 1 and the hyperbola \frac{x^2}{16} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1, respectively. If b < 5 and e_1 e_2 = 1, then the eccentricity of the ellipse having its axes along the coordinate axes and passing through all four foci (two of the ellipse and two of the hyperbola) is :
questions.solution:
1. For the vertical ellipse \frac{x^2}{b^2} + \frac{y^2}{25} = 1 (since b < 5, major axis is along y-axis):
e_1^2 = 1 - \frac{b^2}{25}

2. For the hyperbola \frac{x^2}{16} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1:
e_2^2 = 1 + \frac{b^2}{16}

3. Given e_1 e_2 = 1 \implies e_1^2 e_2^2 = 1:
(1 - \frac{b^2}{25})(1 + \frac{b^2}{16}) = 1

1 + \frac{b^2}{16} - \frac{b^2}{25} - \frac{b^4}{400} = 1 \implies \frac{9b^2}{400} = \frac{b^4}{400} \implies b^2 = 9

4. Find the foci:
- Ellipse: e_1 = \sqrt{1 - \frac{9}{25}} = \frac{4}{5}. Foci are along y-axis at (0, \pm b_0 e_1) = (0, \pm 5 \times \frac{4}{5}) = (0, \pm 4).
- Hyperbola: e_2 = \sqrt{1 + \frac{9}{16}} = \frac{5}{4}. Foci are along x-axis at (\pm a_0 e_2, 0) = (\pm 4 \times \frac{5}{4}, 0) = (\pm 5, 0).

5. New ellipse passing through (\pm 5, 0) and (0, \pm 4):
\frac{x^2}{25} + \frac{y^2}{16} = 1

Its eccentricity is:
e = \sqrt{1 - \frac{16}{25}} = \frac{3}{5}

questions.text:
Let the system of equations

x + 5y - z = 1
4x + 3y - 3z = 7
24x + y + \lambda z = \mu

\lambda, \mu \in \mathbf{R}, have infinitely many solutions. Then the number of the solutions of this system, if x, y, z are integers and satisfy 7 \le x + y + z \le 77, is :
questions.solution:
For infinitely many solutions, \Delta = 0:
[[1, 5, -1], [4, 3, -3], [24, 1, \lambda]] = 1(3\lambda + 3) - 5(4\lambda + 72) - 1(4 - 72) = 3\lambda + 3 - 20\lambda - 360 + 68 = -17\lambda - 289 = 0 \implies \lambda = -17

\Delta_1 = [[1, 5, -1], [7, 3, -3], [\mu, 1, -17]] = 1(-51 + 3) - 5(-119 + 3\mu) - 1(7 - 3\mu) = -48 + 595 - 15\mu - 7 + 3\mu = 540 - 12\mu = 0 \implies \mu = 45

Now let z = k. From the first two equations:
x + 5y = 1 + k
4x + 3y = 7 + 3k

Multiplying first equation by 4:
4x + 20y = 4 + 4k
Subtracting: 17y = k - 3 \implies y = \frac{k - 3}{17}

Then x = 1 + k - 5y = 1 + k - \frac{5k - 15}{17} = \frac{17 + 17k - 5k + 15}{17} = \frac{12k + 32}{17}

Sum of variables:
x + y + z = \frac{12k + 32}{17} + \frac{k - 3}{17} + k = \frac{13k + 29 + 17k}{17} = \frac{30k + 29}{17}

For x, y, z to be integers, k - 3 must be a multiple of 17, so k = 17m + 3 for integer m.
Then x + y + z = \frac{30(17m + 3) + 29}{17} = 30m + \frac{90 + 29}{17} = 30m + 7.

Given 7 \le x + y + z \le 77:
7 \le 30m + 7 \le 77 \implies 0 \le 30m \le 70 \implies 0 \le m \le \frac{7}{3}

Since m \in \mathbf{Z}, m can be 0, 1, 2 (corresponding to k = 3, 20, 37).

Thus, there are exactly 3 integer solutions.

questions.text: If the sum of the second, fourth and sixth terms of a G.P. of positive terms is 21 and the sum of its eighth, tenth and twelfth terms is 15309, then the sum of its first nine terms is :
questions.solution:
Let the G.P. be a, ar, ar^2, \dots with a > 0, r > 0.

1. \text{T}_2 + \text{T}_4 + \text{T}_6 = ar + ar^3 + ar^5 = ar(1 + r^2 + r^4) = 21
2. \text{T}_8 + \text{T}_{10} + \text{T}_{12} = ar^7 + ar^9 + ar^{11} = ar^7(1 + r^2 + r^4) = 15309

Dividing the two equations:
\frac{ar^7(1 + r^2 + r^4)}{ar(1 + r^2 + r^4)} = \frac{15309}{21} \implies r^6 = 729 = 3^6 \implies r = 3

Substitute r = 3 into the first equation:
a(3)(1 + 9 + 81) = 21 \implies 3a(91) = 21 \implies 273a = 21 \implies a = \frac{21}{273} = \frac{7}{91} = \frac{1}{13}

Sum of first 9 terms:
\text{S}_9 = \frac{a(r^9 - 1)}{r - 1} = \frac{\frac{1}{13}(3^9 - 1)}{3 - 1} = \frac{19683 - 1}{13 \times 2} = \frac{19682}{26} = 757

questions.text: If the function f(x) = \frac{\tan(\tan x) - \sin(\sin x)}{\tan x - \sin x} is continuous at x = 0, then f(0) is equal to _____.

If \int (\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{x^3})(\sqrt[23]{3x^{-24} + x^{-26}}) dx = -\frac{\alpha}{3(\alpha + 1)}(3x^\beta + x^\gamma)^{\frac{\alpha+1}{\alpha}} + \text{C}, x > 0, (\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in \mathbf{Z}), where C is the constant of integration, then \alpha + \beta + \gamma is equal to _____.

For t > -1, let \alpha_t and \beta_t be the roots of the equation ((t+2)^{\frac{1}{7}} - 1)x^2 + ((t+2)^{\frac{1}{6}} - 1)x + ((t+2)^{\frac{1}{21}} - 1) = 0. If \lim_{t \to -1^+} \alpha_t = a and \lim_{t \to -1^+} \beta_t = b, then 72(a + b)^2 is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
Let y = t + 2. As t \to -1^+, y \to 1^+.

The sum of roots is:
\alpha_t + \beta_t = -\frac{(t+2)^{1/6} - 1}{(t+2)^{1/7} - 1} = -\frac{y^{1/6} - 1}{y^{1/7} - 1}

Taking limit as y \to 1:
a + b = \lim_{y \to 1} (\alpha_t + \beta_t) = -\lim_{y \to 1} \frac{y^{1/6} - 1}{y^{1/7} - 1} = -\frac{1/6}{1/7} = -\frac{7}{6}

Then:
72(a + b)^2 = 72 (-\frac{7}{6})^2 = 72 \times \frac{49}{36} = 2 \times 49 = 98

questions.text: Let the lengths of the transverse and conjugate axes of a hyperbola in standard form be 2a and 2b, respectively, and one focus and the corresponding directrix of this hyperbola be (-5, 0) and 5x + 9 = 0, respectively. If the product of the focal distances of a point (\alpha, 2\sqrt{5}) on the hyperbola is p, then 4p is equal to _____.

The sum of the series 2 \times 1 \times {}^{20}\text{C}_4 - 3 \times 2 \times {}^{20}\text{C}_5 + 4 \times 3 \times {}^{20}\text{C}_6 - 5 \times 4 \times {}^{20}\text{C}_7 + \dots + 18 \times 17 \times {}^{20}\text{C}_{20}, is equal to _____.
